paragraphs.en: I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.
paragraphs.zh: 最近得知一些科学家希望缩减自己的研究，以减少碳排放，我感到十分震惊。他们说，危机已经来临，我们需要减少能耗巨大的建模工作。至少，我们需要使能源使用变得可持续得多。

paragraphs.en: It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites—the tools we scientists need to measure the planet's pulse—demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science's unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world's electricity.
paragraphs.zh: 无可争辩的是，我们的实验室、科学仪器、火箭和卫星——这些都是我们科学家监测地球脉搏所必需的工具——在建造和运行过程中都需要消耗大量能源。同样确凿的是，科学对信息永无止境的渴求，导致世界各地高耗能数据中心的数量迅速增长。据国际能源署统计，这些设施如今消耗了全球约1%的电力。

paragraphs.en: However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can't track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it's coming from and who's producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这是我们为了解世界而必须付出的代价。如果我们无法追踪大气中的二氧化碳含量、它来自哪里以及是谁排放的，又如何向决策者说明减少碳排放的最佳方式呢？技术研究产生的碳排放是值得的：这些研究最终将保障我们这个星球的未来。

paragraphs.en: It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity's greatest challenges.
paragraphs.zh: 科学家可能很难把这个道理讲清楚，因为我们的工作十分复杂，往往在不对外开放的环境中进行，而且并不总是容易解读或解释。但如果我们要解决人类面临的最大挑战，证明科学的实际效用将至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world's solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world's carbon emissions.
paragraphs.zh: 认识到科学和工程能够带来的希望，是设立千年技术奖的动力。如今，这一表彰人类创造才智的奖项正迎来第20个年头。澳大利亚新南威尔士大学的马丁·格林教授是往届获奖者之一，他发明了钝化发射极和背面电池技术，如今世界上大多数太阳能电池板都采用了这项技术。得益于他的发明，我们真正有了减少全球碳排放的机会。

paragraphs.en: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe's largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.
paragraphs.zh: 每天，科学家、技术专家和工程师都在发现利用可再生能源的新方法，并开发相关技术，不仅让我们更明智地使用能源，也为我们的智能运算提供能源。芬兰的LUMI就是一个很好的例子：它是欧洲最大的超级计算机，令人惊讶的是，它实现了负碳排放。这台超级计算机设在一座旧造纸厂内，由附近的一条河流供电，其远程供热为周边卡亚尼镇的居民提供温暖。

paragraphs.en: If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.
paragraphs.zh: 如果世界要实现净零排放的目标，我们就必须认真思考，如何实现可持续计算，并建成更多像LUMI这样的超级计算机。
